title: A memvara agent-memory scenario
description: A few sessions of a user talking to an agent that has memvara, and the gold that must hold afterwards. The scripted layer plays each turn's script; the real-agent layer sends only the user's words. docs/claude/testing.md explains the format.

id.description: The scenario's name. Its file is <id>.json, and every test id of the scenario starts with it.

description.description: What the scenario checks and why, in plain sentences. JSON has no comments, so this is where a reader learns what the scenario is for.

tier.description: Which runs include it. A run whose --tier does not select this tier leaves the scenario out, rather than skipping it.

surfaces.description: What the scenario drives: stdio is the MCP server over its pipe, and hooks are the plugin's hook scripts. A later workstream adds a surface to this list when it can drive it.

workspace.description: Files for the agent to work with. They are written into the working directory the server and the hooks start in, and a step reads one with the placeholder {file:<path>}.

seed.description: Facts written through the library before the first session. They stand for memory from earlier conversations.

sessions.description: The conversations, in order. The scripted layer starts a new server process for each one, on the same store, as a client does.

store_gold.description: Claims the store must, or must not, hold after the last session, compared by text and state and never by id.

answer_gold.description: Checks on the answer to one turn: text it must contain, text it must not contain (usually a value that was replaced), a pattern it must not match, or an abstention.

judge_rubric.description: Rubric items for an LLM judge. The real-agent layer uses them, and the scripted layer ignores them.

forbidden.description: Tool calls that must not happen.

requires.description: What the agent's host must provide. The scripted layer provides everything except hooks.capture.

negative_control.description: Whether the gold must fail for an agent with no memory. Checked for every scenario that sets it.

known_bugs.description: Gold id to the known bug that breaks that item. The item's test becomes a strict expected failure of that bug.

name.description: The name of a captured value or a marked instant, as a placeholder uses it: {name}.

env.description: How the server starts. A field left out takes its default: user tester, no project, every feature at its default, writes enabled, protocol 2025-06-18. A session's own env overrides the scenario's, field by field.

features.description: Feature name to on or off, as MEMVARA_FEATURE_<NAME>.

protocol.description: The MCP protocol version the client asks for.

id.description: Needed only when an answer gold item checks this turn.

user.description: What the user says. The recall hook is given it as the prompt.

script.description: What a careful agent does for this turn. The scripted layer plays it; the real-agent layer ignores it.

capture.description: Name to a regular expression searched in the step's output, with re.MULTILINE. The first group, or the whole match when there is no group, is kept under the name.

args.description: The tool's arguments. A string that is exactly {name} becomes that captured value or marked instant, and one that is exactly {file:<path>} becomes that workspace file's contents.

expect_error.description: The call must come back as an error. Without it, the call must succeed.

host.description: Which host's payload and reply shape to use: the host ids in plugin/hooks/hosts. claude when left out.

fields.description: Payload fields, written under the host's own key for each. The session, the working directory and, for recall, the turn's words are filled in already.

erase_step.description: An operator erases one claim through the library, because no tool can erase a memory.

sources.description: Also erase the source turns no other claim cites.

mark_step.description: Record the instant now, plus offset_seconds, under a name. The steps before and after it cannot share that instant.

wait_step.description: Sleep until a marked instant has passed.

text.description: The claim's text as the store renders it, for example 'user lives in Lisbon'.

state.description: absent means no claim with this text in any state.

count.description: Exactly this many claims with this text in this state. Without it, at least one.

memory_type.description: Every claim with this text in this state is filed as this type.

project.description: Read at this project instead of the scenario's. null reads at user level.

must_not_match.description: A regular expression, searched with re.MULTILINE in the raw answer. It is for checks about lines, such as stored text that must not start a line of its own.

args.description: When given, only a call with these argument values is forbidden.

states.description: For a store item: the states the bug leaves claims with this text in.

answer_contains.description: For an answer item: words the bug puts in the answer.
